title: Sometimes I Freeze
author: Johny Takkedasila
text:
Sometimes I freeze,
Turned into stone,
Cast into darkness.
On the breath,
Someone has thrown glass shells.

We call it injury—
It is liberation for blood,
Sinking into soil
From the prison of the body,
An unstoppable festival.

The freezing of time is like
The loss of motion in me.
Words fly from the lips,
Graves of memories on the heart,
Followed by a rope of tears.

To move the body,
Well of tears should be dug
By cracking eyes.
Put fire on the tongue
And burn the words;
To the blood, I have to teach the feelings—
A weapon that liquefies anyone:
Fire.

When you see sculpture,
Rain stops.
It was an involuntary act
That my body melted
Into rainwater.

It doesn`t matter though,
You,
Who are the cause of motion in me—
Tearful greetings.
